newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Estonia stocks fall, market still directionless.
newsitem.headline: Estonia stocks fall, market still directionless.

text.p: Trade on the Estonian bourse on Wednesday was quiet but still nervous with no evident trend, dealers said.
Total volume on the official list was down to 42.6 million kroons and the index closed 0.45 percent lower on 250.78.
"The market mood was nervous and it is expected to stay that way, with no clear mood winning out in the direction of the market," one trader said.
Uhispank was most active with 11.1 million kroons of shares turned over to ease by 0.65 kroons to close on 56.30 kroons.
"It difficult to commment on the interest in Uhispank, some of the volume may have gone through the bank's own traders and it was not seen on the market," one trader said.
Hoiupank saw trade of 10.7 million kroons of shares to end 0.75 kroons lower on 126.00 kroons.
"It seems that the results were not good enough to over come the desire to sell by some investors, who had hoped the market would go higher on the results news," a trader said.
"The nervous selling presure was on the market most of the day and kept pulling the price down," another dealer said.
Hoiupank said its Q1 profit was 40.2 million kroons and its March profit was 14.2 compared to February's 12.5 million kroons.
Hansapank was lightly traded on 10.4 million kroons of shares changing hands. It shed 0.50 kroons to 256.00 kroons.
Thomson Bank Watch released a credit rating of BBB for Estonia and for Hansapank an intra-country issuer rating of IC-B and a short-term local currency rating of LC-1.
"Hansapank's price is already high, and I don't think that the price can go higher on this news," one dealer said.
On the free market, total trade was 4.2 million kroons of shares with Rakvere meat plant the most active stock.
Rakvere turned over 1.4 million kroons of shares to close 0.05 kroons lower at 16.10 kroons.
"There is some good consumer market possibilities for Rakvere so it could easily move higher but the general nervous mood is not allowing it to rise," one trader said.
